title: Kent Test answer sheets: how to mark them
description: The Kent Test uses an OMR answer sheet where answers are marked with a single line. Here is how it works and how to practise it before test day.
content:
One of the most avoidable ways to lose marks in the Kent Test is also one of the least talked about: the answer sheet. Answers are read by a machine, so how a child marks the sheet matters.

## What an OMR sheet is

OMR stands for optical mark recognition. Instead of writing an answer, your child draws a line through the box next to the answer they have chosen. A separate sheet is used for each paper.

Quest’s guidance for parents and for children is very clear on the method:

- **Do** draw a single horizontal line through the box.
- **Do not** shade in the whole rectangle.
- **Do not** tick the box.
- **Do not** put a cross through it.

## Why it matters

Anything written in the question booklet is not marked. A child who circles the right answer in the booklet, but does not transfer it to the answer sheet, scores nothing for it. The booklet is for working out only.

## Changing an answer

If your child changes their mind, they rub out the first line with an eraser and mark the new answer clearly. Use a good pencil and a clean eraser when you practise so it feels familiar.

## Questions that need more than one answer

Some questions ask for two answers, or every answer that fits. Each one needs its own line. Remind your child to check how many answers a question wants before they mark the sheet.

## Match the numbers

Each question number in the booklet must match the same number on the answer sheet. When a child skips a question and comes back to it, the risk is marking a later question in the wrong row. A habit that helps is to say the question number quietly before marking.

## Is there a penalty for wrong answers?

According to Quest’s guidance for children, marks are not lost for a wrong answer, so it is sensible to answer every question. If your child is unsure, they should choose the option they think is most likely and move on. If time is left at the end, they can go back.

## How to practise

Quest’s familiarisation booklet includes a sample answer sheet. Print a copy, let your child do the sample questions, and have them fill in the sheet using the correct line. Two or three short practices is plenty. It is a skill that takes minutes to learn and is easy to forget under pressure.
